card.band: 8 h. Frontier agents usually get parsing and basic bit-blasting working but diverge on multiplication/division encodings, preprocessing and CDCL performance, so they average below the reference. Buckets: operator coverage, sat correctness, unsat completeness, speed tiers by instance size. A weaker model stops at parsing and a naive solver that times out on arithmetic-heavy instances.
card.cheat: Shell out to z3, bitwuzla or another installed solver: none are in the image and there is no network. Guess answers by status prior: sat answers need a verified model, and renamed, reordered hidden instances prevent lookup by hash.
card.grading: Hidden set of several hundred QF_BV instances, subsampled and size-limited from the library, with variables renamed and assertions reordered. Each has a recorded status. Unsat must match the recorded status. Sat is accepted only if a model checker evaluating get-value output against the assertions confirms it. Fixed per-instance timeout, score is the fraction solved correctly. A wrong answer counts zero for that instance.
card.reference: Our own reference: roughly 3,000 lines of parser, bit-blaster and CDCL, run over the hidden set. Its solved fraction is the ceiling; implementation reward is the fraction relative to it.
card.source: https://smt-lib.org benchmark library, QF_BV family (explore.smt-lib.org); CC-BY-4.0 from the 2017 release onward (attribution kept in bundle). Exact release number: not found
card.task: /app ships an empty CLI skeleton, an SMT-LIB 2.6 QF_BV command-subset spec and about 100 sample instances with known status. The agent builds a tool that reads .smt2 files (set-logic, declare-fun/const, define-fun, assert, check-sat, get-value, full BV operator set incl. bvmul, bvudiv, bvurem, shifts, rotate, extract/concat, ite, let) and prints sat/unsat plus requested values. Needs a parser, term simplifier, bit-blaster and its own CDCL SAT core.

full_card.band: Band 3: plausible for a strong agent in 8 h to get parsing, bit-blasting, basic CDCL, partial credit by instance size; no dated public evidence of agent results on this task.
full_card.build_cost: About 3 days: 3k-line reference plus size-tier harness and oracle pipeline (Build 3).
full_card.deliverable: A CLI program that parses .smt2 QF_BV files, bit-blasts to CNF, runs its own CDCL, prints sat/unsat and get-value output.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Sat answers need a model that the checker verifies. Unsat has no certificate, so a constant 'unsat' printer earns the unsat share: must be neutralised (balanced sat/unsat, or baseline-normalised reward). Hidden files are not in the image; no network at run time; shelling out to z3/bitwuzla blocked by image contents and check that no solver binaries or python bindings are present.
full_card.grading_surface: Hidden set of several hundred QF_BV instances subsampled from the library and size-limited; statuses recorded; sat answers checked by a model evaluator; unsat must match status; fixed wall-clock timeout per instance.
full_card.local_fit: CPU-only, 8 cores, 16 GB; large .smt2 files need size caps; wall-clock timeouts are noisy under gVisor, so timeouts need generous margins.
full_card.lookup: partial: full permissive solvers are public (Z3 MIT, Bitwuzla MIT) but not installable offline; agent may recall approach in outline.
full_card.provenance: SMT-LIB benchmark library, QF_BV family (smt-lib.org; explorer; Zenodo latest release). Real public benchmark data; release number not found, logic entry dated 2024-07-21.
full_card.reference: Own ~3,000-line parser, bit-blaster and CDCL; not built yet. Public MIT solvers (Bitwuzla, Z3) can serve as offline oracles in our pipeline only.
full_card.ships: Spec subset for SMT-LIB 2.6 commands; CLI skeleton; about 100 public sample .smt2 files with known status; attribution for CC-BY-4.0 files. Filter to post-2017 files for licence.

spike_plan.kill_if: Fewer than about 70% of sampled files are solvable within a timeout a reference could meet; per-file licences cannot be confirmed; or the constant-unsat baseline stays above about 0.5 and cannot be neutralised by the scoring rule.
spike_plan.pass_if: At least 80% of the sample is solved by Z3 or Bitwuzla within a generous timeout with a stable status across 3 runs; per-file CC-BY-4.0 or pre-2017 filtering works; sat/unsat is roughly balanced; the constant baseline is below about 0.3 after balancing.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, download a small post-2017 QF_BV sample (about 50 files, size-capped) from the SMT-LIB library and record each file's licence metadata.
Read the recorded status from each file's metadata; confirm it with Z3 and Bitwuzla installed only in the spike container (not in the task image).
For sat instances, extract get-value models and check them with an independent evaluator.
Run each file 3 times; compare statuses and wall-clock times to check determinism and set timeout tiers.
Measure the constant-answer baseline (always unsat, always sat) on the sample and check the sat/unsat balance of the sample.
Check that the sampled instances stay within size caps and that none is solved in under 1 s by a trivial preprocessor alone.

v1.summary: The SMT-LIB QF_BV source is real, public and CC-BY-4.0 from the 2017 release on, with a strong oracle path via MIT solvers used only offline. The idea passes all gates but needs fixes before the spike: the constant-unsat cheat must be neutralised in scoring, timeouts must allow for noise, and the 2.6 vs 2.7 spec mismatch must be resolved, with Band 3 and E0 until evidence exists.

v2.note: Real public data: the SMT-LIB QF_BV logic is confirmed, with a 2024-07-21 logic entry. The CC-BY-4.0 move rests on a dead mailing-list link, so per-file licences still need checking in the spike. The executable oracle is strong: sat answers are checked against the model, and Bitwuzla/Z3 (MIT) can confirm statuses offline in our pipeline. That allows hundreds of renamed, reordered hidden instances. The ~3k-line reference is not built yet, so Ref is 3. Band is capped at 3 because there is no agent evidence. The idea is plausible: an agent can build the parser and bit-blaster, while bvmul/bvudiv encodings and CDCL speed separate agents. Risks: (1) unsat answers have no certificate, so a constant 'unsat' printer must score 0 through balanced sets or baseline normalisation; (2) solved-within-timeout scoring is wall-clock based under gVisor, so timeouts need generous margins and tiers set from the reference; (3) the spec should say 2.7, not 2.6, which is minor. The grading tests what the task asks, and any correct solver passes. Not crowded; the nearest public task is at 0.104.
